decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's authentication and secure communication base in a growing market, it is likely to stay unless clear early sales fall below aspiration levels.
This fits the firm's move toward mobile interactions and digital signing, so boundedly rational management would usually give it more time rather than withdraw it quickly.
Because it builds directly on the firm's core security architecture capabilities and supports its broader platform position, it is unlikely to be removed after only one year.
It is related to the existing offer but more niche, so management would keep it for now while monitoring whether its results justify continued resource use.

Although close to the established offer, a hardware token is less aligned with the firm's app-centered direction and would be a plausible candidate for problemistic reallocation if early demand disappoints.
Regulatory and compliance-focused security solutions fit the firm's capabilities and customer base well, making continued support more likely than early withdrawal.
